question.text: What will the first reported revenues after October 2026 be for Snowflake?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the total revenue in conformity with US generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) reported in Snowflake's first official quarterly [earnings release](https://investors.snowflake.com/news/default.aspx) covering its Q3 FY 2027, expected to be released in December 2026.
question.fine_print: Only the initially reported figures encompassing the entirety of the quarter will be considered. Any subsequent revisions, corrections, or restatements will not affect resolution.

## Snowflake Q3 FY2027 total revenue: research notes

Snowflake guides only product revenue, so the bin boundaries need translating. Total revenue is product revenue plus about $55M of professional services. Landing exactly on the guidance midpoint gives roughly $1,645M total. Repeating the last two quarters' beats gives roughly $1,720 to $1,725M, which sits right at the $1,725M boundary.

### 1. Resolution source
- 2026-09-02: The Q2 FY27 release (quarter ended July 31, 2026) reported, in thousands:
  - Total revenue $1,546,793, up 35% year on year
  - Product revenue $1,491,861
  - Professional services and other $54,932
  - Q3 FY27 guidance: product revenue of $1,588M to $1,593M (37% to 38% growth) and non-GAAP operating margin of 15.5%. There is no guidance for total revenue.
  [Seeking Alpha PR](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20639002)
- Snowflake says Q3 FY27 results will come out on December 2, 2026, after market close. I got a 403 error from the company page, so the date comes from search snippets and other coverage. [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/fy27-q3-earnings-date-announcement/), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/snowflake-jumped-25-ai-drove-054912152.html)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The quarter ended October 31, 2026, and the results are not out. I found no update to guidance during the quarter.

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: UBS cut its price target to $450 from $500 because of valuation, and kept its Buy rating. It said demand for CoCo (the new name for Cortex Code) and data-migration trends are still healthy. The stock was at about $273, down 9.4% over the week. [Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ubs-cuts-snowflake-stock-price-target-on-valuation-to-450-93CH-5712162)
- 2026-11-18: Short interest fell 6.4% to 17.44M shares as of October 30. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/short-ideas/26/11/63394326/snowflake-short-interest-falls-ahead-of-q3-earnings)
- Undated, written before December 2: Morgan Stanley expects Q3 product revenue of about $1.64B, which it says is about $45M above consensus (implying consensus near $1.595B). With about $55M of services, that implies total revenue near $1.695B. [Finimize](https://finimize.com/content/morgan-stanley-sees-snowflake-beating-q3-guidance-again)
- Aggregators disagree on total-revenue consensus:
  - MarketBeat: about $1.65B
  - Investing.com: about $1.57B, which looks stale since it is below guidance
  - Other aggregators: up to about $1.685B
  
  [MarketBeat](https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/SNOW/earnings/), [Chartmill](https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/SNOW/estimates)
- 2026-09-02: Full-year FY27 product guidance went up to $6,070M from $5,840M. Net revenue retention was 126% and remaining performance obligations were $9B. [Pulse2](https://pulse2.com/snowflake-q2-fiscal-2027-revenue-rises-35-to-1-55-billion-as-product-revenue-guidance-is-raised/)

### 4. Base rates (beats on product revenue, actual vs top of guidance)
| Quarter | Guidance | Actual | Beat vs top |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 FY26 | $1,195M to $1,200M | $1,226.6M | +$27M (+2.2%) |
| Q1 FY27 | $1,262M to $1,267M | $1,334.3M | +$67M (+5.3%) |
| Q2 FY27 | $1,415M to $1,420M | $1,491.9M | +$72M (+5.1%) |

- From memory, not checked this session: in FY26 Q1 to Q3 the beats were roughly $30M to $50M (about 3% to 5%).
- Professional services revenue has been flat at $53M to $57M a quarter (Q1 FY27 was $56.6M and Q2 FY27 was $54.9M). [Snowflake IR Q1](https://investors.snowflake.com/news/news-details/2026/Snowflake-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-2027/default.aspx), [Q4 FY26](https://investors.snowflake.com/news/news-details/2026/Snowflake-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-of-Fiscal-2026/)
- Total revenue implied by different outcomes, assuming $55M of services:

| Product revenue outcome | Product | Implied total | Bin |
|---|---|---|---|
| At the guidance midpoint | $1,590M | ~$1,645M | >$1,615M & <$1,670M |
| Beat of $27M (like Q4 FY26) | $1,620M | ~$1,675M | ≥$1,670M & ≤$1,725M |
| Morgan Stanley estimate | $1,640M | ~$1,695M | ≥$1,670M & ≤$1,725M |
| Beat of $72M (like Q2 FY27) | $1,665M | ~$1,720M | ≥$1,670M & ≤$1,725M |
| 5.3% beat (like Q1 FY27) | ~$1,677M | ~$1,732M | >$1,725M & ≤$1,785M |

- Total revenue grew sequentially by about 8.7% in Q1 FY27 and 11.2% in Q2 FY27. Growth of 8% to 11% on $1,546.8M gives $1,670M to $1,717M.
- Revenue below $1,615M would require missing product guidance, and Snowflake has not missed in the recent history above.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "Snowflake Q3 Product revenue above __?" (fetched 2026-11-19), covers product revenue rather than total, so add about $55M:

| Product threshold | Approx. total equivalent | Yes price |

| >$1.58B | ~$1.635B | 0.845 |
| >$1.62B | ~$1.675B | 0.585 |
| >$1.66B | ~$1.715B | 0.57 |
| >$1.70B | ~$1.755B | 0.28 |

  The prices for >$1.62B and >$1.66B are nearly the same, which looks inconsistent and suggests thin liquidity. Taken together, the implied median for product revenue is about $1.66B to $1.67B, or about $1.715B to $1.725B total, right at a bin boundary.
- Kalshi, customers with trailing 12-month revenue over $1M in Q3: about 870 is roughly 50/50. This is a related market, not about revenue.
- I found no Manifold or Metaculus market on total revenue.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-12-02, after market close: the Q3 FY27 earnings release, which decides the question.
- Before then, analyst previews (for example Zacks key-metric previews) could update consensus. I found no scheduled company event, such as an investor day, before the release.

## Snowflake Q3 FY2027 (quarter ended Oct 31, 2026): research brief

### 1. Resolution source
- Resolution uses total GAAP revenue from the Q3 FY27 earnings release on Snowflake's IR news page. Snowflake says it will publish the release **after U.S. markets close on Wednesday, December 2, 2026**, with the call at 2 p.m. PT. Some aggregators list Nov 30 or Dec 1, but the company's date overrides them. [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/fy27-q3-earnings-date-announcement/)
- Snowflake guides only **product revenue**, not total revenue. Total revenue is product revenue plus professional services and other revenue, which has run at about $54-57M a quarter.
- I found no leading data series of higher frequency. Snowflake does not publish monthly consumption figures.

### 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The quarter has ended but has not been reported.
- 2026-09-02: Q3 FY27 guidance is **product revenue of $1,588M-$1,593M**, up 37-38% year over year. Adding about $55M of services implies total revenue of roughly **$1,643-1,650M** if Snowflake lands exactly on guidance. That falls in the ">1,615 & <1,670" bin. [SA/press release](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20639002)
- 2026-09-02: Full-year FY27 product revenue guidance was raised to $6,070M from $5,840M. [SA/press release](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20639002)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: UBS cut its price target to $450 from $500 and kept a Buy rating. It cited valuation, and said demand for Cortex Code (CoCo) and data-migration trends "remain healthy". The stock was at $272.94, down 9.4% over the week. [Investing.com](https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/ubs-cuts-snowflake-stock-price-target-on-valuation-to-450-93CH-5712162)
- 2026-11-18: A Seeking Alpha piece rates the stock Hold on valuation and notes strong Cortex Code adoption and a growing RPO base. [SA](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4969345-snowflake-record-growth-at-hefty-premiums-profit-taking-risks-maintain-hold)
- 2026-11-18: Short interest fell 6.4% to 17.44M shares (5.16% of float) as of Oct 30. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/short-ideas/26/11/63394326/snowflake-short-interest-falls-ahead-of-q3-earnings)
- 2026-11-02: Snowflake announced the Dec 2 reporting date. [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/fy27-q3-earnings-date-announcement/)
- 2026-09-02: Q2 FY27 was the third straight quarter of faster product revenue growth. Net revenue retention was 126%, RPO about $9B, and EPS $0.62 against a $0.45 consensus. [Herald](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10863372), [SaaStr](https://www.saastr.com/5-interesting-learnings-from-snowflake-at-6-billion-in-revenue-37-growth-and-accelerating-126-nrr-and-a-gross-margin-guided-down-to-pay-for-ai/)

### 4. Base rates (actual product revenue vs. top of guidance; total revenue)
- Q3 FY26 (reported 2025-12-03): product $1,158.4M vs. guidance top of $1,130M, a **+2.5%** beat. Total revenue was about $1.21B (I believe about $1,212.9M). [Nasdaq/RTT](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/snowflake-loss-narrows-q3)
- Q4 FY26 (reported 2026-02-25): product $1,226.6M vs. $1,200M top, **+2.2%**. Total was $1.28B. [Snowflake IR](https://investors.snowflake.com/news/news-details/2026/Snowflake-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-of-Fiscal-2026/)
- Q1 FY27 (reported 2026-05-27): product $1,334.3M vs. $1,267M top, **+5.3%**. Total was **$1,391.0M**, with services at $56.6M. [Snowflake IR](https://investors.snowflake.com/news/news-details/2026/Snowflake-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-2027/default.aspx)
- Q2 FY27 (reported 2026-09-02): product $1,491.9M vs. $1,420M top, **+5.1%**. Total was **$1,546.8M**, with services at $54.9M. [SA/press release](https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20639002)
- Sequential growth in total revenue: Q4 to Q1 was +8.7%, and Q1 to Q2 was +11.2%.
- Here is what those beat sizes imply for Q3 total revenue, assuming about $55M of services. This is arithmetic, not a forecast:
  - A +2.2-2.5% beat gives about **$1,680-1,690M**.
  - A +5.1-5.3% beat gives about **$1,725-1,732M**, right at the 1,725 bin edge.
  - Growing 11.2% from Q2 again would give about $1,720M.
- Year-over-year check: 37-38% product growth on Q3 FY26 means about $1,588-1,599M of product revenue.

### 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket, "Snowflake Q3 Product revenue above __", ends 2026-12-02. Yes prices: $1.58B 0.845; $1.62B 0.585; $1.66B 0.57; $1.70B 0.28; $1.74B 0.052.
  - This market is on **product** revenue, not total, so add about $55M to compare it with this question.
  - The $1.62B and $1.66B prices are nearly the same, which suggests the market is thin or inconsistent.
- Kalshi markets on the count of customers with more than $1M in trailing revenue center around 870 for Q3. They are related but say nothing directly about revenue.

  - At the Q2 report, consensus for Q3 product revenue was about $1.5B, below the guidance Snowflake then issued. [Herald](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10863372)
- I could not find any Manifold or Metaculus market on this question.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-12-02, after market close: the Q3 FY27 earnings release, which resolves the question.
- No pre-announcement or mid-quarter guidance update turned up in my searches. Snowflake has not historically pre-announced results.
- Analyst previews and estimate revisions may come out the week before Dec 2, but they would not change the reported figure.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 13 days. Q3 FY27 results are due December 2, 2026, after market close. The quarter itself ended October 31, so the revenue figure is already fixed and simply not yet reported.

(b) **Status quo:** If Snowflake lands exactly on its guidance midpoint ($1,590M product plus about $55M services), total revenue is about $1,645M, which falls in bin B. However, Snowflake has beaten the top of its product guidance every quarter in recent history, so the realistic status quo is a beat. Repeating the last two beats ($67M to $72M above the top) gives about $1,720M to $1,730M total, right at the C/D boundary.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Beats versus the top of product guidance were +$27M, +$67M and +$72M in the last three quarters.
- In earlier Q3s the beats were smaller: about +$30M in Q3 FY26 and about +$37M in Q3 FY25 (from memory, not checked this session). A Q3-sized beat of $30M to $40M gives a total of about $1,678M to $1,688M, which is bin C.
- There have been no misses in recent history, so total revenue at or below $1,615M (a product miss of roughly $30M) is very unlikely.
- Professional services revenue is stable at $53M to $57M a quarter.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-09-02: Q3 product guidance was set at $1,588M to $1,593M after a $72M beat. Full-year guidance was raised by $230M, net revenue retention was 126% and remaining performance obligations were $9B.
- Morgan Stanley's undated preview, written before December 2, expects about $1,640M product, implying about $1,695M total (bin C).
- Polymarket (2026-11-19, thin liquidity) implies a total median near $1,715M to $1,725M. It puts about 28% on total above $1,755M and about 41% on total below $1,675M. The tails look wider than history suggests, and the near-identical prices at two thresholds look inconsistent.
- 2026-11-18: UBS said demand for CoCo and data-migration trends are still healthy.
- Sequential growth of 8% to 11% gives $1,670M to $1,717M total.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** AI-driven consumption (CoCo, migrations) accelerates enough for product revenue to beat by about 8%, putting product near $1,720M and total above $1,785M. Alternatively, consumption optimizations by large customers shrink the beat to under $20M, putting the total in bin B.

**Weighting:** I start from the historical beat distribution, which centres on a total around $1,700M to $1,715M. Smaller Q3-seasonal beats pull towards C. I then blend towards Polymarket's somewhat higher median and fatter tails, which shifts some probability into D and keeps meaningful weight on B. I discount the market partly because of its thin liquidity.

Option_A: 0.03
Option_B: 0.15
Option_C: 0.46
Option_D: 0.31
Option_E: 0.05

(a) **Time left:** About 13 days. Snowflake reports Q3 FY27 on December 2, 2026, after market close. The quarter ended October 31, 2026, so revenue is already fixed but not yet known.

(b) **Status quo:** Snowflake guided product revenue of $1,588M to $1,593M. Adding roughly $55M of professional services gives about $1,645M total at the midpoint, which falls in the second bin. But the company's habit is to beat guidance, so the "status quo behaviour" outcome is a beat. That points to roughly $1,690M to $1,725M total, the third bin.

(c) **Base rates:** Snowflake has beaten the top of its product guidance in every recent quarter.
- The last three beats were +$27M, +$67M and +$72M.
- FY26 beats were roughly 3% to 5%, from memory and not checked this session.
- A miss below guidance, which the first bin would require, has not happened in recent history.
- Repeating those beats gives total revenue of about $1,675M to $1,732M. Most of that range is in the third bin, with some spill into the fourth.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **Q2 FY27 results (Sep 2, 2026):** Snowflake beat the top of guidance by $72M and raised full-year product guidance to $6,070M. Q3 guidance assumes growth speeding up to 37% to 38%.
- **Morgan Stanley preview (undated, before December 2):** It expects product revenue of about $1.64B, which implies about $1.695B total.
- **Polymarket (Nov 19):** Prices imply a product median of about $1.66B to $1.67B, or about $1.715B to $1.725B total. The prices are internally inconsistent, which suggests thin liquidity.
- **UBS (Nov 18):** It says CoCo demand and data-migration trends are still healthy.
- **Professional services:** These have been steady at $53M to $57M a quarter.

(e) **Unexpected outcomes:**
- **Small beat:** Consumption slows, for example customers optimise spend or AI workloads shift elsewhere. A beat of only about $15M to $20M would put total revenue near $1,660M, the second bin.
- **Large beat:** Strong AI and CoCo consumption produces a beat of 7% or more. Product above $1,700M would push total revenue past $1,755M, into the fourth bin or even the fifth.

**How I got here:** I started from the base-rate beat distribution, which centres total revenue near $1,705M. The Polymarket median of about $1,715M to $1,725M pulls slightly toward the fourth bin. I discounted the market somewhat because it is illiquid and inconsistent: its $1.62B price implies about a 41% chance of a beat under $30M, which looks too high. I kept meaningful weight on both neighbouring bins.

(b) **Status quo outcome:** Snowflake guides product revenue at $1,588M to $1,593M. Adding about $55M of services, landing exactly on guidance gives roughly $1,645M total, which is Option B. However, Snowflake routinely beats its guidance. The "status quo behavior" is another beat of $50M to $75M, which gives about $1,695M to $1,720M total, which is Option C.

(c) **Base rates:**
- Snowflake has beaten the top of its product guidance in every recent quarter.
- The beats were +$27M (Q4 FY26), +$67M (Q1 FY27) and +$72M (Q2 FY27).
- In FY26 the beats were roughly 3% to 5%.
- A miss (Option A) has not happened in recent history.
- Beats of 2% to 5% place total revenue between about $1,675M and $1,732M. That range is mostly Option C and slightly into Option D.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- 2026-09-02: Q2 FY27 total revenue was $1,546.8M, with services of $54.9M. Q3 product guidance is $1,588M to $1,593M. Full-year guidance was raised by $230M, net revenue retention is 126%, and remaining performance obligations are $9B.
- Before the release, Morgan Stanley expects product revenue of about $1.64B, implying about $1.695B total, in Option C.
- 2026-11-19, Polymarket on product revenue:
  - The market prices product revenue above $1.66B at 0.57 and above $1.70B at 0.28.
  - That implies a median product revenue near $1.66B to $1.67B, which is about $1.715B to $1.725B total. That is right at the boundary between C and D.
  - Prices are inconsistent between $1.62B and $1.66B, which suggests thin liquidity. The market also puts real weight, around 40%, on product revenue below $1.62B. That is the Option B region.
- 2026-11-18: UBS cut its price target on valuation but said demand is healthy. The stock fell 9% in a week, a mild caution signal.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:**
- AI-driven consumption (CoCo, migrations) accelerates as it did in Q2, when sequential growth was 11%. A repeat gives product revenue above $1.73B and total above $1.785B (Option E).
- Alternatively, a consumption slowdown or optimization wave could make Snowflake land only slightly above guidance, putting total in Option B.

**How I got from base rate to forecast:**
- From the base rate of recent beats, my starting point was a centre near $1,710M total, with an uncertainty of about $30M either way.
- I moved some weight toward Option B because the Polymarket market prices a meaningful chance of product revenue below $1.62B, and because the stock has been weak recently.
- I kept substantial weight on Option D because the two most recent beats, if repeated, land right at the $1,725M boundary.
